subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Andy Goldsworthy is known for sculpture made from...
options: Natural materials such as leaves, stone and ice in the landscape
questions.explain: Andy Goldsworthy creates ephemeral land art using natural found materials in the environment.

questions.q: 'Product design' is the discipline of...
options: Designing functional objects people use, such as appliances and furniture
questions.explain: Product design develops functional, manufactured objects, balancing how they work and look.

questions.q: In ceramics, building a pot by stacking and joining rolls of clay is called...
questions.explain: Coiling builds a vessel by layering and smoothing rolled ropes (coils) of clay.

questions.q: What does 'firing' clay in a kiln do?
questions.explain: Firing heats clay to high temperatures, turning it permanently hard and durable.

questions.q: Throwing is a ceramics technique that uses...
options: A potter's wheel to shape clay
questions.explain: Throwing shapes clay into rounded forms by hand as it spins on a potter's wheel.

questions.q: What is 'slip' in pottery?
options: Liquid clay used to join pieces or decorate
questions.explain: Slip is clay mixed with water to a creamy liquid, used as a glue or for decoration.

questions.q: 'Welding' is a construction method used mainly with...
questions.explain: Welding fuses pieces of metal together using heat, a common method in metal sculpture.

questions.q: Plaster is most commonly used in 3D work for...
options: Casting solid forms in a mould
questions.explain: Plaster is poured into moulds where it sets, making it a common casting material.

questions.q: A 'relief' sculpture is one where...
options: Forms project from a flat background
questions.explain: In relief, the design is raised from (or sunk into) a flat background rather than standing free.

questions.q: A 'slab' building technique in ceramics uses...
options: Liquid clay poured into a mould
Flat sheets of clay joined together
questions.explain: Slab building cuts and joins flat sheets of clay to make boxes and angular forms.

questions.q: Corrugated card is useful in 3D work because it is...
options: Lightweight, strong and easy to score and fold
questions.explain: Corrugated card is light yet rigid, and can be scored and folded to build 3D forms.

questions.q: A 'glaze' on ceramics provides...
options: A glassy, often waterproof and decorative coating
questions.explain: A glaze melts in the kiln to form a glassy surface that seals and decorates the pot.

questions.q: In 3D design, a 'maquette' or model is made to...
options: Test and plan ideas before making the final piece
questions.explain: A model or maquette lets a designer test scale, form and ideas before committing to the final work.

questions.q: In 3D work, 'armature' refers to...
options: An internal supporting framework for a sculpture
questions.explain: An armature is the internal skeleton, often wire, that supports a modelled sculpture.

questions.q: A sculpture designed to be viewed from all sides 'in the round' is...
options: A relief carved into a flat background
questions.explain: Sculpture in the round is freestanding and can be walked around and viewed from every angle.

questions.q: Which method would a sculptor use to make a hollow form from sheet material?
options: Construction by folding and joining sheets
questions.explain: Folding and joining sheet material is a construction method that can create hollow 3D forms.

questions.q: Which material is shaped while soft and then fired hard in a kiln?
questions.explain: Clay is modelled while soft, then fired in a kiln to become hard and permanent.

questions.q: Joining materials together to make a 3D form is called...
questions.explain: Construction (or assembly) builds a 3D form by joining separate pieces together.

questions.q: 'Architecture' is a branch of design concerned with...
questions.explain: Architecture is the design of buildings and the spaces people use.

questions.q: In 3D design, 'structure' refers to...
options: How a form is built and held together to stay stable
questions.explain: Structure concerns how a 3D object is constructed and supported so it stands and holds together.

questions.q: Which material is most suitable for bending into a flowing linear 3D form?
questions.explain: Wire is easily bent and twisted, making it ideal for linear, gestural 3D forms.

questions.q: Which is an example of three-dimensional design in everyday life?
options: A product such as a chair
questions.explain: Product design, such as a chair, is a form of three-dimensional design.
